detect2 / post-prediction evaluation

IMU displacement versus held-out truth

Specific force is rotated into ENU with supplied attitude, gravity is removed, and acceleration is integrated with zero initial position and velocity in each window. The rotating antenna offset is added before sampling at GNSS epochs. Truth is accessed only after IMU predictions have been saved.

Unknown initial velocity gives linear drift in raw displacement. “Observable” here means after the same quadratic removal used by the detector, not a correction available to full navigation. No true initial velocity, position, bias or generated phase trend initializes the IMU estimate. Attitude is supplied, not estimated.

64 compared windows; 64 matching IMU/oracle decisions; 24 conclusive in both modes. Maximum observable displacement RMSE: 197.6 micrometres.

Detector fits and decisions · Comparison summary · Per-window motion/phase errors and gamma

Gray: held-out truth. Purple: IMU estimate. Right: estimated minus true. Displacement uses Axis; phase uses Signal. Actual propagation directions are used only for phase evaluation when present in held-out truth, otherwise the plot explicitly uses nominal satellite geometry.

Controlled errors were injected into the supplied IMU/attitude inputs; settings and seed are recorded in run.json. Attitude is still supplied rather than estimated. Known antenna offset and common nominal timebase are assumed. These are engineering sensitivity experiments, not measured hardware performance. The original full-3D classifier and quality thresholds are unchanged.
